Tonight's trap work, to rate: ten TrapLab maps (one per kind of trap, ten stations each: TL-SPIKE-01 to TL-TRIGGER-10), ten TrapGaunt gauntlets (TG-01 to TG-10: 5 to 14 stages in a row, rest rooms between; seven with monsters that rise as you go, three pure traps) and ten TrapDemo missions (TD-01 to TD-10: medium maps with a camp, a quest giver, a boss from the BossLab, a main quest and a side quest, and trap passages between the rooms). All thirty are installed: TLSpike ... TLTrigger, TrapGnt01 ... TrapGnt10, TrapDem01 ... TrapDem10 in the map list.

Each picture is the station or the whole map as the editor draws it (zoom in: the pictures are sharp). The caption says what the trap is, its tier (standard: any class with some skill; hard: it punishes mistakes), how it is meant to be passed, and what testing found. 'In the game' numbers come from OpenNox itself: a probe walked the hero through every station along the simulator's careful route and along a careless straight walk and run, and the game's traps did the damage.

What the game test cannot show: the probe moves the hero by script, so it cannot be shoved and walls do not stop it (pushers and closing walls were also walked with real input, the game's own physics: see the morning report), and for a jump it steps the hero over the jump's frames. Spells, triggers and motion detection that the simulator only partly models were judged by the game's numbers and by reading the scripts.
Rate as in the QA rounds: 1-5, keep / fix / drop, a note on anything; a note per set at the top of each set. A station that is too easy, unfair, unreadable or dull is exactly what to flag.
